sections.h2: What should Scott County, Illinois owners know about property tax?
sections.html:
Scott County is one of the smallest counties in Illinois, so its tax offices are lean and most questions go straight to a handful of courthouse departments in Winchester. The county seat is at 35 East Market Street, and the county was formed on February 16, 1839 from part of Morgan County, with a name borrowed from Scott County, Kentucky.

The 2020 count was 4,949 residents, which made it the fourth-least populous county in the state. The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 4,866, a 4.1% drop from its estimates base. About 251 square miles of land spread that population out to roughly 20 people per square mile, and the Illinois River forms the western boundary. Morgan County lies to the east, Greene to the south and Pike to the west.

  • Housing units, July 1, 2025 estimate: 2,377
  • Typical home value among owners in the 2020 to 2024 survey: $96,400
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 79.0%, with a median gross rent of $689
  • Median household income: $66,705
  • Residents 65 and older: 26.4%
  • Employer establishments in 2023: 84, with total employment of 604

sections.h2: Which Scott County offices handle assessments, bills and records?
sections.html:
Three offices cover most property tax questions: the Assessor, the Treasurer and the County Clerk. Each has a page on the county website at scottcoil.gov, and each does a separate job in the yearly cycle.

  • The Assessor (Supervisor of Assessments) applies exemptions, maintains the parcel numbering system and the county map files, sends assessment notices, runs the appeal process and certifies the roll to the County Clerk. The office phone listed on the exemptions page is 217-742-5751, and the email is assessor@scottcoil.gov.
  • The Treasurer coordinates collection of real estate and mobile home taxes, keeps the revenue records, disburses the money to taxing bodies and answers parcel questions by phone or in person.
  • The County Clerk, working with the Treasurer, helps run the annual sale of delinquent taxes. The county site also lists property records and fee schedule pages for deed and record requests.

The assessor's fee list was updated on April 27, 2026. A property record card costs $1.00, copies are $0.50 per page, a printed 8 1/2 by 11 aerial map is $10.00 and an emailed PDF aerial map is $5.00. Pull the record card before a listing, because it shows the characteristics the assessment is based on.

sections.h2: When are Scott County property tax installments due?
sections.html:
Scott County collects in two installments, and the Treasurer posts the dates each year at the top of its page. For 2026, the bills were mailed on June 8, the first installment was due July 17 and the second was due September 18. Both dates have passed, so check with the Treasurer's Office for the schedule on the next bill.

Scott County 2026 tax milestones published on county pages

Source: Scott County Treasurer and Scott County exemptions page.

Illinois taxes are billed a year behind. As the DuPage County Treasurer explains it, taxes for 2025 are billed and collected in 2026, so a house sold in the fall still has the current year's bill ahead of it for the following spring. Mobile home taxes run through the same Treasurer's Office and are billed separately from real estate.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can lower a Scott County tax bill?
sections.html:
Exemptions reduce the equalized assessed value, and Scott County lists several on its exemptions page. Owners apply through the Chief County Assessment Office, which also handles the renewal forms.

  • General homestead: the increase in assessed value above the 1977 level, up to $6,000 in counties that do not touch Cook County.
  • Senior citizens assessment freeze: a 2025 law signed on December 12, 2025 (Public Act 104-0452) raises the maximum household income starting with the 2026 assessment year payable in 2027. After the 2028 year the limit stays at $79,000 unless the General Assembly changes it. Applicants submit a federal income tax return with all schedules.
  • Returning veterans: a $5,000 reduction for two consecutive tax years, filed on Form PTAX-341.
  • Persons with disabilities: a $2,000 annual reduction, renewed each year on Form PTAX-343-R.
  • Standard exemption for veterans with disabilities: $2,500 at a service-connected rating of 30% but under 50%, $5,000 at 50% but under 70%, and full exemption at 70% or more, provided the property's total value is under $250,000.
  • Specially adapted housing for a veteran with a disability: a reduction of up to $100,000.
  • Homestead improvement: up to $75,000 of added fair cash value ($25,000 assessed) for four years after a remodel or rebuild is finished and occupied.

sections.h2: How can a Scott County owner appeal an assessment?
sections.html:
A written complaint is filed with the Board of Review inside 30 calendar days of the assessment list's publication. That window is set by 35 ILCS 200/16-55(d). Mail counts as filed on the postmark date, and a courier counts on the date shown on its tracking label.

The statute tells the board to review compulsory sales, including those the complainant submits, if they match the property's characteristics and condition. Start with the Assessor's record card and ask why the value changed. Then gather recent sales of similar Scott County houses, which is the evidence a board looks at first. The decision can go to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board if you disagree. An appeal tests the assessed value only, because tax rates are set by the taxing districts.

sections.h2: What happens when Scott County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The Treasurer, assisted by the County Clerk, holds an annual sale of delinquent real estate taxes, delinquent mobile home taxes and unpaid special assessments. A parcel that stays unpaid can therefore be sold to a tax buyer.

Call the Treasurer's Office for the balance on the parcel, the sale date and any prior year left open. Redemption steps and costs come from the County Clerk, so request a written payoff figure instead of relying on an estimate. A buyer's title company will run the same search, so settle any open year before you list.

sections.h2: How does a house sale work in Scott County when tax is still owed?
sections.html:
Owed tax does not stop a sale, but it must be paid or settled at closing so the buyer receives a clean title. The title company or closing attorney typically requests a payoff from the Treasurer, takes the amount from the seller's proceeds and files the deed with the county.

  • The state transfer tax in 35 ILCS 200/31-10 runs 50 cents on each $500 block of stated value, and a transfer declaration (PTAX-203 or MyDec through the Department of Revenue) goes with the deed.
  • Ask the County Clerk about local recording fees and any county stamp rate before closing day.
  • The 2020 count lists 12.0% of the county's 2,388 housing units as vacant, so a buyer comparing parcels has many options.

Owners who inherited a house, lack funds for repairs or are behind on taxes can list, sell privately or take an as-is cash offer. The last route can close without repairs, and the payoff is handled at the closing table in the same way as any other sale.

faqs.q: Where is the Scott County, Illinois courthouse?
faqs.a: The county seat is Winchester, and the county website gives the address as 35 East Market Street. The Treasurer, Assessor and County Clerk each have their own page at scottcoil.gov.

faqs.q: When were Scott County property taxes due in 2026?
faqs.a: Installment one fell on July 17, 2026 and installment two on September 18, 2026, after bills went out June 8. The Treasurer's Office can give the next set of dates.

faqs.q: How much is the Scott County general homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The county page says the maximum is $6,000 in counties not contiguous to Cook County, measured as the increase in equalized assessed value over the 1977 amount.

faqs.q: What is the filing window for an assessment complaint in Scott County?
faqs.a: You have 30 calendar days after the assessment list is published. File in writing with the Board of Review, and keep proof of the postmark or tracking label.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Scott County house if the property tax is unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid amount is requested from the Treasurer as a payoff and settled at closing from the sale proceeds, so the buyer receives clear title.
